home.title: Your home. One system.
home.description: Kyrion brings devices, services and your information together in a local, modular platform. Explored today through a working home prototype, with a team environment in development. AI assistance is optional.
home.heroNote: Development prototype, not generally available. Shared household events, roles and invitations are implemented; real family use, voice quality and recovery still need acceptance.
home.diagramCaption: An ecosystem vision. Core validates actions across every interface; voice is evolving and automations are planned.
home.connectionDescription: Bring selected devices and services into one understandable place. Start with the controls that work today.

connectionCards.title: Rooms & lighting
connectionCards.description: Organise rooms and control selected Nanoleaf, Zigbee and Bluetooth lights.

connectionCards.title: Calendar & media
connectionCards.description: Joint household events, voluntary calendar sharing, Spotify Connect and YouTube links.

connectionCards.title: People & access
connectionCards.description: One HOME or BUSINESS Space per installation, roles and revocable invitations. Optional central identity preserves local login.

home.worksTitle: One platform between you and your home.
home.worksDescription: You decide what should happen. Velora and other interfaces help you express it. Kyrion Core understands the request, checks it and connects it to your devices and services.

worksVelora.title: Web & optional voice
worksVelora.description: Use the Web interface today. Velora voice reliability is still being validated.

worksCore.title: Kyrion Core
worksCore.description: Checks identity, permissions and action policy, then records execution results.

worksEnvironment.title: Your home
worksEnvironment.description: Selected lighting, sensors and media through bounded integrations.

worksCloud.title: Cloud when you need it.
worksCloud.description: Optional services, separate from the local foundation.

home.worksNote: Local functions remain independent wherever practical. Individual integration availability is limited in the prototype and shown separately.
home.localCloudEyebrow: LOCAL FIRST. CLOUD WHEN YOU WANT IT.
home.localCloudTitle:
Your infrastructure.
Your choice of connections.
home.localCloudDescription: Kyrion itself does not depend on cloud accounts. Devices, rooms, central settings and local functions stay in your own system wherever practical.

localCard.label: YOUR SYSTEM
localCard.title: The foundation stays local
localCard.description: Kyrion is built for local processing and storage. A traditional server or NAS is not required – a suitable local computer is enough for the relevant use case.

cloudCard.label: OPTIONAL CONNECTION
cloudCard.title: Services are added when you need them
cloudCard.description: Personal Google calendars can be shared voluntarily as availability or details. Household events can be sent manually to opted-in personal destinations. Spotify, Google and optional cloud AI require their providers and network access; YouTube uses a visible browser player.

home.permissionsDescription: Core enforces installation-wide roles and validates device actions. Optional AI proposes requests through the same controlled path. Room and device permission scopes remain planned.
home.integrationsEyebrow: FOR THE THINGS YOU ALREADY USE
home.integrationsDescription: Implemented means present in the development prototype, not a consumer release. Hardware evidence covers selected devices; it does not establish compatibility with every device in an ecosystem.
home.hardwareTitle: Do you need your own server?
home.hardwareDescription: Core, Web and PostgreSQL need a configured local host. Local AI and speech add separate runtime and hardware requirements.

hardwareFaq.question: Can I install Kyrion with one command?
hardwareFaq.answer: Not yet. Installer v1 has an implemented fresh-install boundary, but its checked-in manifest contains no installable artifacts. Signed release acceptance, certificates, backup/restore verification and a clean Raspberry Pi rehearsal remain open.

hardwareFaq.question: What already runs on local hardware?
hardwareFaq.answer: Core, Web and PostgreSQL form the local platform. A Raspberry Pi gateway supports selected lighting and voice paths. Local AI and speech use separately configured providers; a Pi-only AI setup is not established.

hardwareFaq.question: Where can I find setup instructions?
hardwareFaq.answer: The repository contains developer startup instructions and the installer implementation status. These are technical setup documents; a supported consumer installation is still in development.

home.featuresTitle:

home.ecosystemTitle:
Many systems.
One place to bring them together.
home.ecosystemDescription: Integrations connect the devices. Core holds the rules. Web, voice and optional intelligence give you different ways to interact—with the same controlled action path.
home.veloraDescription: Velora is Kyrion’s developing voice interface. Local chat, wake detection, transcription and bounded device actions exist. Physical dialogue, word endings, continuity and latency still need repeatable acceptance. Spoken interruption is not implemented; AI remains optional.

Transparent in development.

capabilities.title: Home control
capabilities.description: Manage rooms, lighting and device state through a common catalog. Nanoleaf, Philips Hue via Zigbee and a bounded Bluetooth light path have working implementations.

capabilities.title: Connected ecosystems
capabilities.description: Native control paths plus a bounded, read-only Home Assistant device/state import. The HA import still awaits physical verification.

capabilities.title: Assistance and model choice (K-AI)
capabilities.description: Local chat, model selection, policies and opt-in personal context are implemented. Ollama has real generation evidence; OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini requests were simulated. With explicit consent, cloud receives only the current message, without personal context sources.

capabilities.title: Shared installations
capabilities.description: One HOME or BUSINESS Space per installation, system/custom roles and revocable invitations. Optional central-account linking preserves independent local password login. Public central sign-in needs separate activation; room/device scopes remain planned.

capabilities.title: Diagnostics & activity
capabilities.description: Service health, explicit device availability and correlated action history. Inspect decisions and execution outcomes without guessing.

capabilities.title: Local infrastructure
capabilities.description: Core, local persistence and a bounded Raspberry Pi gateway form the current foundation. Cloud providers are optional capabilities.

capabilities.title: Velora & voice
capabilities.description: Wake detection, transcription and multi-turn voice paths exist. Audio quality, session ending, continuous playback and acoustic latency remain open acceptance work. Spoken barge-in is not implemented.

capabilities.title: Automations
capabilities.description: Future scheduled and event-driven workflows through Core policy. A general automation builder and execution platform are not available.

capabilities.title: Broader integrations
capabilities.description: Versioned plugin contracts, richer Home Assistant capabilities and more device ecosystems. A public marketplace is not implemented.

capabilities.title: Calendar & Lounge
capabilities.description: Create household events with selected participants and edit them jointly. Share personal calendar availability or details voluntarily, and manually send selected events to approved Google destinations with individual status and retry. Deleting a household event retains personal copies. Real family/provider acceptance is open; recurring and all-day authoring remain planned. Spotify Web receiver acceptance is open; YouTube uses the visible browser player.

capabilities.title: Installer v1
capabilities.description: Not yet. Installer v1 has an implemented fresh-install boundary, but its checked-in manifest contains no installable artifacts. Signed release acceptance, certificates, backup/restore verification and a clean Raspberry Pi rehearsal remain open.

capabilities.title: Your documents (K-Data)
capabilities.description: Personal PDF/text upload and local retrieval with sources are integrated. Real local-model answers, hostile-document limits and recovery of nonempty document storage still need acceptance. Shared team knowledge, OCR and cloud document context are unavailable.

capabilities.title: Spaces for home and business
capabilities.description: HOME/BUSINESS setup, roles, invitations and optional mailbox/domain verification are integrated and software-tested. Only one Space runs per installation. Multi-Space operation, Business Voice and complete Business isolation acceptance remain unavailable.

about.title:
Your home should work
on your terms.
about.description: Kyrion is a local-first intelligent home platform, built to bring fragmented devices and services into one understandable system.
about.introTitle:
One intelligent layer.
Not another isolated ecosystem.
about.intro: A connected home can still feel disconnected. Lights, sensors and services each bring their own app, account and rules. Kyrion exists to make those systems work together without giving up control over the infrastructure underneath.
about.paragraph: The goal is a coherent orchestration layer above specialised systems. Integrations provide connectivity. Core manages authority. People choose how to interact.

principles.title: Local first, by intention
principles.description: Process and store information close to the home wherever practical. Essential functions should remain usable without AI or an always-on cloud connection.

principles.title: Ownership that means control
principles.description: Keep external providers optional and transparent. Make permissions, data destinations and consequential actions understandable.

principles.title: Useful before impressive
principles.description: Prove small, complete capabilities on real systems. Treat working code, automated tests and physical verification as different forms of evidence.

about.visionTitle: A foundation for the long term.
about.vision: Over time, Kyrion aims to connect more of the home: devices, media, energy systems and personal services. The direction is ambitious; each addition must earn its place through useful, controllable behaviour.
about.origin: The first user is its creator. The prototype is shaped by real local infrastructure and daily use, with broader validation still ahead.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy | Kyrion
privacy.intro: How Kyrion processes information on its public website and through its product and connected services.

sections.title: Responsible party and contact
sections.body: Kyrion is responsible for this website. Contact: hello@kyrion.ch.

sections.title: Website access data
sections.body: Hosting and security systems may process your IP address, request timestamp, requested URL or resource, browser and user-agent information, and server or security logs. Processing and retention depend on the actual hosting and security configuration.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Information entered in the contact form, and messages sent to hello@kyrion.ch, are processed to answer and follow up on your inquiry. Please do not send passwords or sensitive personal details.

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
sections.body: The site stores your theme preference in localStorage under kyrion-website-theme. Sign-in uses a short-lived HttpOnly flow cookie and a protected HttpOnly session cookie that can keep you signed in for up to 30 days. The central identity provider also uses its own sign-in cookies. Contact-form drafts are not stored.

sections.title: Optional website account
sections.body: Website sign-in uses the central identity provider and a separate website session database. The website stores a generated account identifier, provider issuer and subject, sign-in and session records, encrypted renewal credentials, and security events. Passwords and email verification are handled by the identity provider. A website account does not grant access to a local Kyrion installation. Website logout, central-provider logout and local installation sessions are separate.

sections.title: Session validity and stored records
sections.body: The website can keep you signed in on your device for up to 30 days. It renews short-lived identity checks with the central sign-in service in the background. This uses a protected session cookie and encrypted renewal credentials in the separate website account database. Signing out ends this website session. Session validity is not a deletion deadline for account and security records or backups. Contact inquiries may remain in the receiving mailbox. For retention or deletion questions, contact hello@kyrion.ch.

sections.title: Analytics and tracking
sections.body: The current public website uses Vercel Analytics for website measurement. It does not include advertising or behavioural marketing trackers such as Google Analytics, Plausible, Matomo or Meta Pixel.

sections.title: Google integrations and Google API data
sections.body: Kyrion may allow users to connect Google services such as Google Calendar. Google access occurs only after explicit authorization. Kyrion requests permissions required for enabled functionality, limits access to functionality requested by the user, and allows users to disconnect or revoke access. Google API data is not sold or used for advertising. Kyrion's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs is intended to adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

sections.title: Local-first architecture
sections.body: Kyrion is designed as a local-first smart-home platform. Data is processed locally wherever practical. External services receive information only when their functionality requires it and the corresponding integration or cloud capability is explicitly used or enabled.

sections.title: Third-party services
sections.body: Explicitly connected providers may process data under their own policies. The public website uses Vercel for hosting and analytics, and its contact channel uses server-side SMTP delivery.

sections.title: Data security
sections.body: Kyrion uses appropriate technical and organizational measures intended to protect information against unauthorized access, loss and misuse.

sections.title: Requests and rights
sections.body: Contact hello@kyrion.ch with questions or requests concerning access to, correction of, or deletion of personal data. Requests are handled according to applicable law.

terms.title: Terms of Service | Kyrion
terms.intro: Terms for using the Kyrion website and publicly available Kyrion services.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: These terms apply to the Kyrion website and publicly available Kyrion services where applicable.

sections.title: Product status
sections.body: Kyrion is currently under development. Features may change, be added, removed or temporarily unavailable. The website does not promise a finished consumer product.

sections.title: Availability
sections.body: Kyrion is provided without a guarantee of uninterrupted or error-free availability.

sections.title: Third-party integrations
sections.body: Google and other external provider features also depend on those providers. Kyrion cannot guarantee their availability or behaviour.

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.body: Do not misuse Kyrion, attempt unauthorized access, interfere with services, exploit vulnerabilities, or use Kyrion unlawfully.

sections.title: Intellectual property
sections.body: The Kyrion website, branding, software and original content remain protected by applicable rights unless otherwise stated. Third-party and open-source components remain subject to their own licenses.

sections.title: Liability
sections.body: Kyrion is provided according to its current development state. Liability is limited to the extent permitted by applicable law.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: These terms may be updated as Kyrion evolves. The current version is published on this page.

private.title:
Your home.
More connected.
private.description: Control lighting, organize events and find information again: Kyrion is bringing these tasks together step by step. You choose which devices, services and AI capabilities to use.
private.notice: Development prototype, not generally available. Shared household events and voluntary calendar disclosure are implemented; real family/provider acceptance remains open.

cases.title: Organize devices and rooms
cases.description: Create rooms, assign devices and control selected lights. Nanoleaf and specific Zigbee/Bluetooth lights have physical evidence. This does not establish support for every model. Home Assistant supplies a bounded device/state import; full hardware acceptance remains open.

cases.title: Bring events and services together
cases.description: Create household events with selected participants and edit them jointly. Share personal calendar availability or details voluntarily, and manually send selected events to approved Google destinations with individual status and retry. Deleting a household event retains personal copies. Real family/provider acceptance is open; recurring and all-day authoring remain planned. Spotify Web receiver acceptance is open; YouTube uses the visible browser player.

cases.title: Choose how assistance helps
cases.description: K-AI provides local chat and bounded command proposals. Confirmed memories, history and a personal calendar can be enabled as context. Velora adds voice; repeatable dialogue reliability still needs validation. A satellite does not identify its speaker and receives no private context.

cases.title: Find answers in your documents
cases.description: Personal PDF/text upload and local retrieval with sources are integrated. Real local-model answers, hostile-document limits and recovery of nonempty document storage still need acceptance. Shared team knowledge, OCR and cloud document context are unavailable.

private.controlDescription: Core manages permissions and validates actions. Basic device controls do not require AI. Local models and document retrieval need separately configured runtimes and suitable hardware. Local first does not mean every connected service runs locally.
private.cloudNote: Google, Spotify and other external services require their own connections. Cloud AI is optional and needs provider access and explicit consent. The current AI path releases only the current message; personal memories, history, calendar and documents are not released as cloud context. Fully local operation of every feature is not promised.
private.setupDescription: Kyrion currently requires technical experience and your own development environment. Web, Core and PostgreSQL are configured separately; AI and voice need additional local services. Supported devices must be reachable on your network and explicitly enrolled. A Raspberry Pi can serve as a gateway, but is not an established replacement for all AI hardware.
private.setupNote: There is no released consumer installer or guaranteed alpha/beta access. Optional central-account code is implemented, but public registration requires separate activation and grants no local Space access. Express interest through the contact channel.
private.ctaTitle: What would help in your connected home?
private.ctaDescription: Tell us about your devices, everyday tasks or a question about development.

business.title:
Devices, services and team knowledge.
One shared direction.
business.description: Kyrion aims to help small businesses and teams connect their digital environment in an understandable way. This area presents the vision and early development, not a production-ready business service.
business.notice: Business is in development. Spaces and identity are integrated and software-tested. Real business operation and complete isolation acceptance remain open. There is no production multi-tenant offering, hosted team environment or guaranteed support.
business.examplesNote: The following examples describe possible future uses, not available business features.

cases.title: Understand the workspace
cases.description: For example, manage lighting, rooms and selected device states in a small office through a common interface. Today’s device capabilities are a starting point; business-specific access rules still need validation.

cases.title: Connect schedules and services
cases.description: For example, bring shared events and connected services into one overview. The current personal calendar and integration capabilities do not establish complete team scheduling or resource booking.

cases.title: Make team knowledge easier to find
cases.description: For example, search internal guides with source references. K-Data starts with personal documents. Shared knowledge, document-level access rules and their connection to Spaces still need implementation and combined validation.

cases.title: Assistance with clear boundaries
cases.description: For example, explain information and propose supported actions. Core remains responsible for permissions and execution. General autonomous workflows, cloud team knowledge and industry-specific acceptance are not current offerings.

business.controlTitle: Access control is a prerequisite, not a promise.
business.controlDescription: The integrated prototype supports one HOME or BUSINESS Space per installation, system/custom roles, revocable invitations, optional mailbox/domain proof and host-local owner recovery. Automated tests cover the integrated software; real business acceptance remains open.
business.cloudNote: Real mailbox/domain acceptance and complete isolation of devices, workers, AI streams and knowledge remain open. Multiple Spaces in one running installation are blocked. Business voice is blocked until per-person authority is established. Optional central identity does not create membership, and public activation has separate operational gates.
business.setupDescription: Prove the intended identity and permission flows, device and document isolation, operation and recovery on the intended runtime. Shared team knowledge and resource booking need separate implementation; household calendars do not establish those business capabilities.
business.setupNote: Subscriptions, billing, a customer portal, managed hosting and privileged remote support are not implemented. No prices or availability dates are announced.
business.ctaTitle: Which use case would you like to connect?
business.ctaDescription: We welcome discussion about concrete needs of small businesses and teams. An inquiry does not establish a service offering or guaranteed access.

download.title: Download and installation
download.description: Get Kyrion for your local network. Setup belongs to the downloaded installer.
download.localOnly: Download here, then configure Kyrion on your own device. Accounts, Spaces, devices and integrations are set up in the installer and managed locally afterward. This website does not collect your installation configuration.
download.unpublished: No accepted installer release has been published yet. Development builds are not offered as supported public downloads. Windows provisioning and platform acceptance are still being completed.
requirements: Linux candidates: Debian 13 on x64 or ARM64, and Raspberry Pi OS 13 on ARM64. These paths still require clean-host and restart acceptance.
Windows x64: native installer packaging is in development. The existing inventory probe is not a working Windows installation path.

The current non-AI Linux candidate requires at least 4 GiB RAM and 12 GiB free storage, plus Docker Engine and Compose v2. The installer will check the actual target. These minimums do not establish AI performance.
Local networking and administrator permission are required for installation. Internet is needed for initial downloads and account linking; local functionality is intended to continue offline.
No extra smart-home hardware, microphone, AI model or paid cloud account is required for the essential local installation.
help: Wait for a published installer matching your supported operating system and architecture. Verify its publisher and release information.
Start the downloaded installer on each intended target. Review the proposed services, permissions and downloads before accepting system changes.
Complete account, local access and Space setup inside the installer. Optional integrations and AI can be skipped and configured later.
Keep your recovery information in a protected place. Configure backups before relying on the installation. Do not expose local services through router port forwarding.

hardware.title: Use the hardware you need.
hardware.description: Understand the building blocks before adding devices. There is no purchase requirement.
hardware.note: The installer checks the actual target and asks what you already own. This page provides information only; it does not configure devices, select a Space or collect a hardware survey.

scenarios.title: Kyrion without additional devices
scenarios.description: Start with the local central services and software features. Extra radios, microphones and AI are optional. Choose a supported always-on device if the household should remain available when a desktop is switched off.

scenarios.title: Existing smart home
scenarios.description: Keep devices paired to Home Assistant or their existing controller. A supported integration connects that inventory to Kyrion. Do not attach a second Zigbee process to a coordinator already used by another service. Compatibility depends on each integration and device capability.

scenarios.title: Optional local AI
scenarios.description: Recommendations must reflect the device that actually runs inference, available RAM and GPU memory, acceleration, disk capacity and concurrent work. A GPU name alone does not prove acceleration support. You can complete setup without AI.

scenarios.title: Optional voice
scenarios.description: Voice needs a suitable microphone and speaker plus explicitly enabled audio processing. A satellite can place capture in another room; the installer must show where wake-word, speech recognition and speech generation run. Audio acceptance is separate from service health.

protocols.title: Zigbee
protocols.description: A radio ecosystem using a coordinator. Existing paired networks remain with their current coordinator and software; importing through Home Assistant does not require pairing every device again.

protocols.title: Matter
protocols.description: An application protocol with a compatible controller. Matter devices may use different supported transports; Matter does not mean that a Zigbee stick can control them.

protocols.title: Thread
protocols.description: An IPv6 mesh network. Thread devices need a compatible Border Router to reach the surrounding IP network. A Thread Border Router and a Matter controller serve different roles.
